newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-BRAZIL RECALL DUNGA FOR FRIENDLY AGAINST MEXICO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZIL RECALL DUNGA FOR FRIENDLY AGAINST MEXICO.

text.p: Midfielder Dunga, captain of Brazil's World Cup winning team in 1994, was recalled to the national team on Tuesday for the first time in nearly two years.

Dunga, better known for his strong personality, leadership and grit rather than traditional Brazilian flair, was among eight foreign-based players chosen by coach Mario Zagallo for a friendly against Mexico in Miami on April 30.

The 33-year-old, who plays for Jubilo Iwota in Japan, had suffered from Zagallo's apparent reluctance to select players who are based in Japan. The last of his 65 full international caps was against South Korea in August 1995, when he scored the only goal of the game.
"What he represented for us in the World Cup was something very special," said Zagallo, who was assistant coach at the time.
Zagallo also ignored reported pleas from Barcelona and called up their star striker Ronaldo for the eighth time since he joined the Spanish club.

Brazilian newspapers claimed Tuesday that Barcelona were angry at losing the services of the highly-paid star so frequently, especially as the games have been friendlies against generally inferior opposition.
The six other players named Tuesday were defenders Andre Cruz and Roberto Carlos and midfielders Flavio Conceicao, Cesar Sampaio, Mauro Silva and Leonardo.
Mexico were the last team to beat Brazil in a full international, when they won the final of the CONCACAF Gold Cup 2-0 in January 1996.
Brazil, who played in the tournament as guests, claim they fielded an under-23 team on that occasion and consider a 2-1 loss to Germany in 1993 as their last full international defeat.
